name: Ironmarrow SoftArmor Ballistic Underlayer
description:
Matte black, form-fitting, worn under street clothes without obvious bulk. The torso shell and upper thigh panels are densely woven shear-thickening gel fiber — pliable at rest, rigid on impact. A faint hexagonal quilting pattern marks the protected zones. Shoulder and side seams are reinforced with ceramic whisker tape.

The neck sits high. Chrome-routing channels run along both inner forearms and the upper spine, finished with snap-close covers. Smells faintly of industrial solvent from the gel impregnation process. Runs warm.
functionality: Rated for fragmentation and low-velocity ballistic protection across torso and upper thighs. Chrome-routing channels allow power and data lines from arm or spinal implants to route cleanly under outer garments. Anti-IR inner coating reduces thermal signature. Does not protect against high-velocity rifle rounds.
what_it_says: You expect to get shot at, and you've planned for it.
worn_by: Tier 2 gang-adjacent workers in hot neighborhoods
story_hooks: A murder victim was wearing an Ironmarrow underlayer — the round that killed them wasn't supposed to penetrate it, which means the shooter used something very illegal.
Ironmarrow units are serialized; the street version has the serial ground off, but forensics can still find the ghost number under UV.
A Tier 2 factory worker quietly wearing one every day hasn't told anyone why — something is coming and they know it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting underlayer that hugs the torso and upper legs like a second skin. The matte black surface is nearly invisible under street clothes, creating an imperceptible silhouette beneath looser wear. The high neckline suggests protective intent without shouting it.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight through the core and thighs, designed for zero bulk and maximum concealability. Allows full range of motion while maintaining contact with skin for optimal impact response.
physical_description.primary_material: Shear-thickening gel-impregnated synthetic weave with ceramic whisker tape reinforcement at stress points
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly tacky surface at rest with an underlying quilted architecture. The hexagonal pattern is subtle but tactile — raised ridges marking each protected zone. Chrome-routing channels feel cool and slightly metallic to the touch.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep matte black throughout, with faint silver-grey hexagonal quilting visible under direct light. Chrome snap covers gleam subtly at forearm and spine junctures.
physical_description.closures: Snap-close covers over chrome-routing channels; body seams are friction-fit and seamless
distinctive_features: Shear-thickening gel fiber in torso and upper thigh — rigid on impact, pliable at rest
Faint hexagonal quilting pattern delineating armor zones
Ceramic whisker tape reinforcement along shoulder and side seams
Integrated chrome-routing channels on inner forearms and upper spine
Industrial solvent scent — signature of gel impregnation
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional with Tier 2 aspirations — street-corponation hybrid manufacturing suggests accessible luxury for working-class professionals, mercenaries, and corpo security contractors
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by street operatives, independent security, corpo mid-level staff, and anyone navigating high-risk zones without full ballistic gear. Signals practical paranoia and street credibility without the obvious aggression of visible armor.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new with industrial smell; develops subtle wear patterns where gel channels see repeated flex. Snap covers may show micro-corrosion after months of use. Remains functionally intact for years.
